assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model identified a clean, simple mechanism (interlayer tunnelling renormalising the Dirac velocity to zero at magic angles), and the experimental discovery of correlated insulation and superconductivity opened the field of moire matter. It is the kind of simple model with universal consequences that I trust, and it has spawned a broad family of tunable correlated platforms.
assessment.attribution: The theory-experiment pairing is natural: Bistritzer and MacDonald for the flat-band prediction, Jarillo-Herrero for the experimental demonstration. Other experimental groups and earlier theory (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) could contest priority, and I cannot independently verify the exact credit history.
assessment.maturity: Correlated-insulator and superconducting phases have been reproduced by many independent groups since 2018, and the flat-band picture is well established. The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, but the discovery itself is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority of the flat-band prediction relative to earlier twisted-bilayer theory is not settled in the supplied text.
The microscopic origin of superconductivity remains unresolved, so the prize would need to be phrased around the platform and correlated phases.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the HgTe observation, reshaped how we classify band insulators and established topology as an organising principle in condensed matter. The idea is conceptually clean and has strongly influenced materials research.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory; Molenkamp led the experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang theory, not credited here). Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators is a further decisive contribution, so the three-person limit forces a choice that I regard as the main allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by many groups over more than fifteen years, with robust interpretation. If anything recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the 3D topological insulator experiments (Hasan, others) or the HgTe experiment should be recognised alongside Kane-Mele is open.
Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and other early contributors are outside the supplied credited names, so the configuration may be incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and its application to random constraint-satisfaction problems and inference connected statistical physics of disordered systems to computer science and learning, giving analytical predictions of phase transitions in satisfiability and algorithmic hardness. It is exactly the sort of mechanism-level, rigorous theory I value, and it ties into current understanding of why learning works.
assessment.attribution: Mézard, Parisi and Virasoro developed the cavity method; Parisi has already been recognised (2021) for spin-glass theory, so Mézard, Zecchina and Montanari are a plausible set but the weight of Mézard versus others and the role of Parisi's earlier prize complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Rigorous results (e.g. proofs of replica predictions) and algorithmic confirmation exist, though some applications are still evolving. The theoretical core is mature, but overlap with the 2021 prize could be seen as partly already honoured.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2021 prize for spin-glass theory may make this look like a second recognition of the same underlying idea.
Whether the core contribution is physics or computer science and applied mathematics could be questioned.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation defines a universality class for non-equilibrium interface growth, and its exact solution and experimental confirmation (liquid-crystal turbulence, Takeuchi and Sano) show a universal, simple mechanism behind messy growth phenomena. Conceptually deep and linked to random matrices (Tracy-Widom statistics), which is close to my own background.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the equation; Parisi is not in the credited names, which leaves an awkward attribution. Takeuchi is credited for the decisive experimental confirmation of the universal distributions. Theory solutions by Sasamoto-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel, Calabrese-Le Doussal are also important and not credited.
assessment.maturity: Strong experimental confirmation of the one-dimensional class and exact results exist; higher dimensions remain open. The interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Omission of Parisi (and of the exact-solution contributors) from the credited names makes a fair configuration difficult.
Broad physical applicability beyond a few experimental systems may be judged limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realising the Hubbard model with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the Mott insulator transition and later quantum-gas microscopy, gives a controllable analogue simulator of strongly correlated many-body systems and a bridge between statistical physics and atomic physics. Clear, high impact on many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch-Zoller-Cirac provided the theoretical proposal and Greiner-Bloch the Mott transition experiment; Esslinger did fermionic Hubbard work. Five credited names exceed three laureates, so choosing among the theory and experiment sides is unresolved; I propose the experimentalists but the theory side is strongly arguable.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed in many groups; the quantum simulation of fermionic Hubbard physics at the lowest temperatures is still incomplete, so scientific payoff for open problems like d-wave pairing is pending.
uncertainties: Theory (Cirac, Zoller) versus experiment (Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger) credit allocation is unresolved.
Overlap with earlier cold-atom prizes (BEC 2001, 2012 trapping and manipulation of quantum systems).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides the architecture for readout and control of superconducting qubits and demonstrates strong light-matter coupling on a chip. It underlies much of present quantum hardware and is conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf are a coherent theory-plus-experiment triple (with Huard, Girvin and others as co-authors of the key 2004 proposal and experiment). Overlap with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits would need to be considered.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and technologically central; the interpretation is stable. The 2025 prize may reduce the room for another superconducting-circuit award soon.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum effects in circuits.
Other key contributors (Girvin, Huard, Devoret-related work) could dilute the credited triple.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's high-accuracy implementation, have improved timekeeping by orders of magnitude and enable precision tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The measurements are well understood and decisively confirmed.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the accuracy frontier; other contributors (Hollberg, Hall for combs, earlier proposals) exist, but a two-person prize is clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature, multiply confirmed, and still advancing with the prospect of a redefinition of the second, which could suggest waiting for it.
uncertainties: Whether a prize is better timed after redefinition of the SI second.
Overlap with the 2005 prize on optical frequency combs and 2012 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture unified the rigidity transition of grains, foams and glasses into a critical-like phenomenon with universal scaling, which is the type of simple mechanism across disciplines that I find compelling. Its direct experimental reach is more modest than the other candidates, and the connection to glasses is partly open.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram and are a natural pair; contributions of O'Hern, Silbert, Wyart and others on isostaticity and critical exponents could be viewed as decisive for the quantitative theory.
assessment.maturity: Numerical and experimental evidence is substantial but the connection to the glass transition and the exact universality are still debated, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Whether the jamming transition is a true critical point with universality is still debated.
Contributors to the quantitative theory (O'Hern, Wyart, Parisi-related mean-field work) are outside the credited names.
